class.name: JRPGCharacterSheet
class.brief_description: Cuts a character sheet into the animations a character is drawn with.
class.description: A character sheet holds one character by default: a row of walk frames for each way it faces, up, right, down and left (then up-right, down-right, down-left and up-left on an 8-direction sheet), with column 0 the standing pose. [method make_frames] turns a sheet into [SpriteFrames] with one animation per direction, named [code]up[/code], [code]right[/code], [code]down[/code], [code]left[/code] (and [code]up_right[/code], [code]down_right[/code], [code]down_left[/code], [code]up_left[/code]). Sheets laid out differently are described by options: [code]frames[/code] (walk frames a row, default 4), [code]directions[/code] (4 or 8), [code]grid[/code] (characters across and down the image, default [code]Vector2i(1, 1)[/code]) with [code]index[/code] (which one, row by row), [code]row_order[/code] (the direction names of the rows, comma-separated), [code]y_offset[/code] (pixels to draw the character higher) and [code]object[/code] (an object that bushes do not hide). The editor's Character Sheet importer (Import As in the Import dock) takes the same options and saves the [SpriteFrames]; an image imported as a plain texture is cut with the default layout.

method.name: get_y_offset
method.description: Returns how many pixels higher than its cell [param frames] are drawn: the [code]y_offset[/code] their sheet was cut with.

method.name: is_object
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] when [param frames] belong to an object (the [code]object[/code] option): bushes do not hide its lower part.

method.name: load_frames
method.description: Returns the frames a character reference is drawn with: [param reference] is a [code]uid://[/code] or [code]res://[/code] path, as database entries hold it. [SpriteFrames] made by the Character Sheet importer come back as they are; an image is cut with the default layout. Returns [code]null[/code] when the file is missing or the image does not fit the default layout.

method.name: make_frames
method.description: Returns the [SpriteFrames] of one character of [param texture], cut as [param options] describe (see the class description; options left out keep their defaults). Returns [code]null[/code], with an error saying why, when the image does not divide into that layout or the options are wrong.
